task: Close PR #1174's explicit scope gap: probe_chunk (engine.py) still fully re-lexed self._prefix + chunk from position 0 on every call. Apply the identical self._fed_last_token_start suffix-anchor strategy PR #1174 used for _incremental_sync, adapted to probe_chunk's read-only contract (must never mutate engine state); prove I3/I6 (probe_chunk's own bool | None return value) byte-identical at every step, not just the final one.

summary: New method _probe_delta_from_anchor(self, chunk) -> list | None: when self._fed_token_count > 0 and self._fed_last_token_start is not None, re-lexes only self._prefix[safe_offset:] + chunk instead of self._prefix + chunk. Compares the re-lexed suffix's first token against self._fed_tokens[boundary_idx]; on a match returns the not-yet-fed delta tokens (suffix_tokens[1:]). Returns None on no-anchor-yet, suffix lex failure, or a changed boundary-token identity -- never guesses, never mutates self.

Deliberately does NOT reconstruct a full fed-token-key list the way _incremental_sync's anchor path does -- probe_chunk never needs keys after computing delta, so skipping that reconstruction avoids reintroducing an O(fed_token_count) cost per probe.

probe_chunk now calls _probe_delta_from_anchor(chunk) first; on success uses the delta directly; on None, falls back to the exact pre-existing full-prefix _lex_tokens(self._prefix + chunk) path with identical downstream checks and _copy_probe_fallbacks bookkeeping.
No change to probe_chunk's external contract (bool | None, side-effect-free), _incremental_sync, _full_sync, _sync, _feed_delta_tokens, or any grammar/terminal definition.
change.why_safe: Identical maximal-munch argument PR #1174 established for _incremental_sync, reused verbatim (not re-derived): every already-fed token except possibly the last is permanently settled once a token after it was recognized. self._fed_last_token_start still names the one uncertain boundary token; re-lexing self._prefix[safe_offset:] + chunk re-derives it (and anything genuinely new after it) exactly as a full-prefix lex would. The two grammar facts PR #1174 verified directly (Token.start_pos/end_pos independent of propagate_positions; no openui.lark terminal uses lookbehind/\b) are unchanged and apply identically -- no new verification needed. On any anchor failure, probe_chunk falls back to the exact pre-existing full-prefix path, which independently re-derives ground truth; so whenever the anchor path returns a value, it is provably identical to what the full path would return.

reproduction.method: self-contained before/after via a monkeypatched _probe_delta_from_anchor that always returns None (forcing full-prefix relex on every probe) -- no git stash needed for the perf/I3-I6 comparison itself; git stash used separately to confirm the new unit tests are not vacuous
reproduction.long_program: Same 543-char, 10-line, multi-statement valid OpenUI DSL program (LONG_PROGRAM) as PR #1174's tests, for direct comparability across the two fixes.
reproduction.drive_pattern: Realistic probe-then-commit drive matching compiler_draft.py's actual usage (branch.probe_chunk(piece) then branch.advance(piece) on a truthy/None result): at each of 543 steps, probe the next single character against the currently-synced prefix without committing, record the bool|None result, then commit it via set_prefix before probing the next character.
reproduction.scripts_not_committed: none -- measurement used inline python -c invocations against the committed test module's own helpers (LONG_PROGRAM, _drive_probe_and_commit, _disabled_anchor, _CharCountingEngine), not a separate scratch script

why_smaller_than_incremental_sync_fix: probe_chunk's per-call chunk in this drive is a single character (the smallest possible unit), narrowing the absolute character-count gap between the anchor and full paths compared to _incremental_sync's PR #1174 drive.

InteractiveParser.copy() plus the delta feed onto the copy are fixed per-call costs this fix does not touch and _incremental_sync does not pay (it mutates self._ip directly); these dilute the relative wall-time win from reduced lex work.
